Finishing a move after the 250 ms of reading: two rules

300 ms rule. If David turned in the window, one more turn counts if it comes at most 300 ms after the gesture start.
Regular-step rule. If David turned in the window, one more turn counts if it comes before David's next regular step after that turn (he has moved only the one cell the turn itself caused).

  • The turns are the ones your recorded game made (the model you played with), at their recorded times. Both boards start from the real game at the gesture start (each example opens about 1.1 s earlier, with the real game; gray line = where David came from). Each board reads the turns of the first 250 ms, then one more turn if its rule allows it; then David goes straight until he eats the harp or dies.
  • Windows here are the proposed ones: a gesture that starts less than 250 ms after a window's start belongs to that window.
  • Score: harp +1; a death costs −0.5, less the later it comes (decay length 1 step for wall and tail, 3.7 for spears); a spear from the side costs nothing. Only spears from attackers already on screen at the gesture start are simulated.
  • Keys: space play/pause, ← → one tick, g gesture start, ↑ ↓ previous / next example.
